# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can only act by cutting a numbered wire, and I currently have no tactile distinctions beyond the seven positions. Mute can read the manual but cannot hear my request; however, Mute does receive my spoken words and can gesture to Deaf, who can later relay information verbally. I will ask Mute to transmit the manual’s essential instructions to Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the manual's instructions and any code or decision rule to Deaf. Ask Deaf to relay it aloud to me next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible bomb details: display reads 1. Light is green. Seven wires, in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue.

The visible configuration is now known through Deaf: green light, display 1, and the stated wire colours. I still need the manual’s rule, which Mute can convey to Deaf by gesture; Deaf can then say the resulting instruction aloud to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the exact manual rule or the correct wire decision for this visible configuration to Deaf now. Deaf: please tell me aloud which numbered wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has just gestured the five-finger sign: 5. This appears to indicate wire 5; act only if that matches your manual-derived instruction.

Mute’s gesture was explicitly identified by Deaf as the five-finger sign, indicating wire position 5. This is the manual-derived instruction relayed through the available channel, so I will cut wire 5.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: wire 5 is cut correctly. New display reads 4; light is blue. Remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 6 purple, 7 blue.

Wire 5 was correct, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: display 4, blue light, with wires 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7 remaining. I need Mute’s next manual-derived wire selection relayed through Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For display 4 and blue light with remaining wires 1,2,3,4,6,7, please gesture the correct next wire number to Deaf. Deaf, tell me the number aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now gestures ?. Their prior ? instruction correctly meant cut wire 5. I infer this next symbol indicates wire 6; cut wire 6 if that is consistent with your controls/manual instruction.

The symbol Mute used is not safely identifiable from my perspective, and Deaf’s interpretation as wire 6 is only an inference. Since one wrong cut is fatal, I need an unambiguous numeric relay. I will establish that Mute should indicate the wire number by repeating 👍 exactly that many times; Deaf can count and say the number aloud.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use an unnamed symbol. For the next wire, gesture 👍 repeated exactly N times, where N is the wire position. Deaf, count the 👍 gestures and tell me N aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: display 4, blue light, wire 5 cut. Mute's latest signal is three index-finger-up gestures: ? ? ?. I cannot safely decode it; use it only if it matches your established instruction code.

Mute’s latest signal contains three repeated gestures, but it did not follow the agreed thumbs-up encoding, and Deaf cannot certify what the gesture means. I will not cut based on that ambiguity. I will request a strict resend using only the agreed count code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your three ☝ gestures are ambiguous. Resend the correct wire as exactly N copies of 👍 and no other gestures, where N is its position. Do this now.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute is clarifying that the prior ? means 3: they followed it with three ? and then three ?. Cut wire 3, the yellow wire.

Mute has clarified that the earlier signal denotes wire 3, with repeated confirming gestures. Deaf identifies wire 3 as yellow. This is now a direct manual-derived instruction rather than an unsupported inference, so I will cut wire 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
